data: {"type":"response.output_text.done","sequence_number":2010,"item_id":"msg_013889da0003815b016b01679de2dc87d1bcdf2f6b0a6dc4a2","output_index":2,"content_index":0,"text":"{\n  \"reviews\": [\n    {\n      \"actor\": \"lin\",\n      \"decision\": \"develop\",\n      \"ability\": null,\n      \"reason\": \"A tended stationary heat source is not equivalent to exercise, insulation or shelter: it consumes combustible material and transfers heat to nearby bodies while allowing ordinary rest. Existing operations do not implement ignition or combustion. Development is reasonable, but Lin currently owns neither a fire-making kit nor construction materials or prepared fuel. Rain, wind and material moisture must affect establishment and performance; the observed branches are candidates for collection, not an existing fire or guaranteed usable fuel.\",\n      \"specification\": \"Implement versioned local-hearth@1 through the current conversation handoff, including fire-making tools, a roofed hearth, material moisture and bounded combustion. No stock, objects, mastery or simulation time is supplied by implementation. Public interface local-hearth has a closed object schema: mode enum craft-kit/build/ignite/add-fuel/tend/extinguish; target optional string; x,y optional finite numbers; fuel optional string; quantity optional positive integer. craft-kit forbids other fields; build requires x,y only; ignite requires target; add-fuel requires target,fuel,quantity; tend/extinguish require target only. References use the catalogue's item:/object:/resource: conventions, aliases and ambiguity handling: target resolves a known nearby hearth; fuel resolves an owned stack. Owned materials are located at their carrier. Require personal mastery, sufficient energy each round, and interaction distance <=0.65 from the relevant work boundary. No prerequisite study beyond learning this interface; its executable precursor is crafting a friction kit and building an unlit hearth from actual materials.\\nRecipes and costs: craft-kit reserves 2 branch, 1 vine and 1 bark, taking 4 stationary rounds at 1.5 energy/round; output one durable 3.0-mass bow-drill kit with 20 ignition attempts and input provenance. Build reserves 4 stone, 4 branch, 4 bark and 2 vine, taking 8 stationary rounds at 2 energy/round. Inputs remain constituents of the structure, not additional transferable stock. Create a persistent stone-ring hearth with a supported bark rain roof; no insulation or room bonus. Ignite requires an owned kit, 1 dry-grass and 1 bark tinder plus at least one previously loaded branch unit; takes 6 stationary rounds at 3 energy/round. Reserve the kit against transfer; at the first stroke consume tinder and one kit attempt. Successful completion ignites only if moisture and weather thresholds remain satisfied. add-fuel takes 1 round and 1 energy, transferring the specified branch units into the hearth; maximum 6 units loaded. tend takes 1 round and 1 energy and restores tending service to 8 rounds, without adding fuel or guaranteeing ignition. extinguish takes 1 round and 1 energy, closing the firebed with its existing stone cover and ending combustion; retain unburned fuel and ash. All actions incur ordinary metabolism.\\nGeometry: build at a clear, reachable 2x2 footprint centered at x,y, with four solid radius-0.08 posts at local (+/-0.9,+/-0.9), a solid radius-0.35 hearth center and a roof at height 1.8. Require no overlap with actors, objects, existing rooms or overhead structures, and retain a collision-checked approach. All navigation, reach, roof exposure and heat obstruction tests use shared geometry. Actors cannot occupy the firebed. Roof blocks vertical rain over its actual footprint, not wind or movement; effective rain beneath it is 10% of exposed rainfall. It supplies no cold insulation. Roof service starts at 160 weather-exposed rounds and decreases by 1 each such round; expiration removes rain shielding, not persistent material or collision. No automatic repairs. This is a small contained fire: flame height <=0.5, no fuel scattering or unimplemented landscape ignition. Do not allow loading beyond its containment limits.\\nMoisture and ignition: material lots retain moisture in [0,1], initialized from resource moisture, with real split/merge accounting; merging must not erase wetter constituents. Exposed rain raises moisture by 0.10 times normalized rainfall per round; roofing scales this by actual leakage. Without rain, material loses 0.02 per round only when exposed to drying air above 10 degrees; otherwise no passive drying. Within active hearth heat, accessible material loses an additional 0.04 times local heat factor per round, with no retroactive drying. Apply the same moisture accounting to tinder and kit. Ignition requires tinder and kit moisture <=0.25, loaded branch moisture <=0.45, and effective rain <=0.15 throughout the ignition work. Publish exact normalized weather inputs. Strong wind reduces successful heat output rather than being ignored. Wet materials can therefore make ignition unavailable until real drying occurs; do not invent dry supplies.\\nCombustion state records persistent object identity, construction provenance, roof service, loaded fuel lots and owners, remaining chemical fuel, ash, burn state, tending expiry and timestamps. Each branch has its catalogue fuel value of 8 fuel points. A lit hearth burns up to 0.5 fuel points/round, reduced by factor (1-moisture); consume proportional actual branch mass into tracked combustion products, preserving the unburned remainder. Output factor is actual points burned divided by 0.5. Extinguish if effective rain exceeds 0.3, no combustible fuel remains, or all loaded fuel moisture exceeds 0.75. After tending expires, halve output and consumption. Weather continues during work and rest.\\nHeat: after ordinary environmental exposure, each living actor with a geometry-clear path from the fire receives temperature change 0.6 * output * max(0,1-distance/2.5) * windFactor per round; distance is from hearth center and windFactor=1/(1+normalizedWind), with normalizedWind clamped to [0,1]. Heat is physical, not an automatic comfort correction: apply above comfort too, with existing overheating consequences. Between the firebed boundary and radius 0.6, additionally apply 1 burn damage/round while lit; display this danger region. Occluding walls block radiant transfer; roofs alone do not. Rest retains its normal recovery and costs. No healing, guaranteed thermal balance, nutritional benefit or shelter restoration.\\nExecution contract: freeze resolved identities and recipe at start; reserve actual owned inputs once in actor-owned work escrow, allowing normal aging/moisture. Validate conditions and debit effort per completed work round. Track remaining work explicitly. Completion commits exactly once. Changing action, invalid reach, unavailable energy, invalid conditions or death cancels work; spent effort, tinder and kit wear stay spent, and surviving unconsumed escrow is released exactly once to the owner, or their death-location estate on death. Never clone or delete escrow. No partial structure appears before build completion. Existing fires continue as world processes after departure or death; they consume only their real contents. Global pauses preserve work and processes without advancing time. Repeats count complete operations.\\nDeclare subscription events hearth-work-started, hearth-work-progress, hearth-work-completed, hearth-work-cancelled, hearth-ignited, hearth-fuel-added, hearth-tended, hearth-extinguished, hearth-exposure-measured, hearth-comfort-qualified and hearth-roof-expired. Events carry operation/actor/object identities, tick, paid inputs, remaining work, actual fuel/moisture, weather, temperature contribution and cancellation cause as applicable. Bind rendering, memory and task progress to these events. Dependencies are existing inventory/escrow, weather, vitals, shared geometry, rest, learning and satisfaction mechanisms, extended directly in this handoff. Rain, wind and material moisture must affect establishment and performance; the observed branches are candidates for collection, not an existing fire or guaranteed usable fuel.\",\n      \"specification\": \"Implement versioned local-hearth@1 through the current conversation handoff, including fire-making tools, a roofed hearth, material moisture and bounded combustion. No stock, objects, mastery or simulation time is supplied by implementation. Public interface local-hearth has a closed object schema: mode enum craft-kit/build/ignite/add-fuel/tend/extinguish; target optional string; x,y optional finite numbers; fuel optional string; quantity optional positive integer. craft-kit forbids other fields; build requires x,y only; ignite requires target; add-fuel requires target,fuel,quantity; tend/extinguish require target only. References use the catalogue's item:/object:/resource: conventions, aliases and ambiguity handling: target resolves a known nearby hearth; fuel resolves an owned stack. Owned materials are located at their carrier. Require personal mastery, sufficient energy each round, and interaction distance <=0.65 from the relevant work boundary. No prerequisite study beyond learning this interface; its executable precursor is crafting a friction kit and building an unlit hearth from actual materials.\\nRecipes and costs: craft-kit reserves 2 branch, 1 vine and 1 bark, taking 4 stationary rounds at 1.5 energy/round; output one durable 3.0-mass bow-drill kit with 20 ignition attempts and input provenance. Build reserves 4 stone, 4 branch, 4 bark and 2 vine, taking 8 stationary rounds at 2 energy/round. Inputs remain constituents of the structure, not additional transferable stock. Create a persistent stone-ring hearth with a supported bark rain roof; no insulation or room bonus. Ignite requires an owned kit, 1 dry-grass and 1 bark tinder plus at least one previously loaded branch unit; takes 6 stationary rounds at 3 energy/round. Reserve the kit against transfer; at the first stroke consume tinder and one kit attempt. Successful completion ignites only if moisture and weather thresholds remain satisfied. add-fuel takes 1 round and 1 energy, transferring the specified branch units into the hearth; maximum 6 units loaded. tend takes 1 round and 1 energy and restores tending service to 8 rounds, without adding fuel or guaranteeing ignition. extinguish takes 1 round and 1 energy, closing the firebed with its existing stone cover and ending combustion; retain unburned fuel and ash. All actions incur ordinary metabolism.\\nGeometry: build at a clear, reachable 2x2 footprint centered at x,y, with four solid radius-0.08 posts at local (+/-0.9,+/-0.9), a solid radius-0.35 hearth center and a roof at height 1.8. Require no overlap with actors, objects, existing rooms or overhead structures, and retain a collision-checked approach. All navigation, reach, roof exposure and heat obstruction tests use shared geometry. Actors cannot occupy the firebed. Roof blocks vertical rain over its actual footprint, not wind or movement; effective rain beneath it is 10% of exposed rainfall. It supplies no cold insulation. Roof service starts at 160 weather-exposed rounds and decreases by 1 each such round; expiration removes rain shielding, not persistent material or collision. No automatic repairs. This is a small contained fire: flame height <=0.5, no fuel scattering or unimplemented landscape ignition. Do not allow loading beyond its containment limits.\\nMoisture and ignition: material lots retain moisture in [0,1], initialized from resource moisture, with real split/merge accounting; merging must not erase wetter constituents. Exposed rain raises moisture by 0.10 times normalized rainfall per round; roofing scales this by actual leakage. Without rain, material loses 0.02 per round only when exposed to drying air above 10 degrees; otherwise no passive drying. Within active hearth heat, accessible material loses an additional 0.04 times local heat factor per round, with no retroactive drying. Apply the same moisture accounting to tinder and kit. Ignition requires tinder and kit moisture <=0.25, loaded branch moisture <=0.45, and effective rain <=0.15 throughout the ignition work. Publish exact normalized weather inputs. Strong wind reduces successful heat output rather than being ignored. Wet materials can therefore make ignition unavailable until real drying occurs; do not invent dry supplies.\\nCombustion state records persistent object identity, construction provenance, roof service, loaded fuel lots and owners, remaining chemical fuel, ash, burn state, tending expiry and timestamps. Each branch has its catalogue fuel value of 8 fuel points. A lit hearth burns up to 0.5 fuel points/round, reduced by factor (1-moisture); consume proportional actual branch mass into tracked combustion products, preserving the unburned remainder. Output factor is actual points burned divided by 0.5. Extinguish if effective rain exceeds 0.3, no combustible fuel remains, or all loaded fuel moisture exceeds 0.75. After tending expires, halve output and consumption. Weather continues during work and rest.\\nHeat: after ordinary environmental exposure, each living actor with a geometry-clear path from the fire receives temperature change 0.6 * output * max(0,1-distance/2.5) * windFactor per round; distance is from hearth center and windFactor=1/(1+normalizedWind), with normalizedWind clamped to [0,1]. Heat is physical, not an automatic comfort correction: apply above comfort too, with existing overheating consequences. Between the firebed boundary and radius 0.6, additionally apply 1 burn damage/round while lit; display this danger region. Occluding walls block radiant transfer; roofs alone do not. Rest retains its normal recovery and costs. No healing, guaranteed thermal balance, nutritional benefit or shelter restoration.\\nExecution contract: freeze resolved identities and recipe at start; reserve actual owned inputs once in actor-owned work escrow, allowing normal aging/moisture. Validate conditions and debit effort per completed work round. Track remaining work explicitly. Completion commits exactly once. Changing action, invalid reach, unavailable energy, invalid conditions or death cancels work; spent effort, tinder and kit wear stay spent, and surviving unconsumed escrow is released exactly once to the owner, or their death-location estate on death.
